'''Billy Howard Sr.'''<ref name="obit"/> (July 17, 1950 – February 13, 2005) was an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[defensive lineman]] who played three seasons with the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the Lions in the second round of the [[1974 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] at [[Alcorn State University]]. Howard also played for the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Early life and college==
Billy Howard was born on July 17, 1950, in [[Clarksdale, Mississippi]].<ref name="Pfa"/> He attended [[Coahoma Agricultural High School]] in Clarksdale.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/howa00600.html | title=BILLY HOWARD | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=November 19, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129035629/http://www.profootballarchives.com/howa00600.html | archive-date=2014-11-29 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Howard was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Alcorn State Braves football|Alcorn State Braves]] of [[Alcorn State University]] from 1970 to 1973.<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/h/howa00600.html | title=Billy Howard | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=22 May 2025}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Howard was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the second round, with the 39th overall pick, of the [[1974 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HowaBi20.htm | title=Billy Howard | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=22 May 2025}}</ref> He officially signed with the team on June 8, 1974.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in 12 games for the Lions during the 1974 season and posted one sack.<ref name="Pfr"/> Howard appeared in 13 games, starting 12, in 1975, recording four sacks and one fumble recovery.<ref name="Pfr"/> The Lions finished the 1975 season with a 7–7 record.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/det/1975.htm | title=1975 Detroit Lions Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=22 May 2025}}</ref> He played in 13 games for the second straight year, starting seven, in 1976 and made one sack.<ref name="Pfr"/> Howard was released by the Lions on 
June 4, 1977, after failing a physical.<ref name="transactions"/>

Howard signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in 1977.<ref name="transactions"/> However, he was later released on August 30, 1977.<ref name="transactions"/>

Howard was then signed by the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/h/howa00600.html | title=Billy Howard Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=22 May 2025}}</ref> He dressed in four games for the Blue Bombers during the [[1977 CFL season]].<ref name="Pfa"/> He dressed in 12 games in 1978.<ref name="Pfa"/> Howard dressed in all 16 games for Winnipeg in 1979 as the team finished 4–12.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/1979cflwpg.html | title=1979 Winnipeg Blue Bombers (CFL) | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=22 May 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Howard was a control operator for the city of [[Fort Worth, Texas]].<ref name="obit"/> He died on February 13, 2005, in [[Grand Prairie, Texas]], at the age of 54.<ref name="obit">{{Cite web|title=Billy Howard Obituary (1950 - 2005) - Grand Prairie, TX - Star-Telegram|url=https://www.legacy.com/amp/obituaries/dfw/3181760|access-date=2021-05-02|website=www.legacy.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''William Joseph Cesare''' (born June 2, 1955) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Miami Dolphins]], and [[Detroit Lions]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis Tigers]] and [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami]]. Cesare also played in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL).

==Early life and college==
William Joseph Cesare was born on June 2, 1955, in [[New York City]].<ref name="Pfa"/> He attended [[Miami Beach Senior High School]] in [[Miami Beach, Florida]].<ref name="Pfa"/>

Cesare was a member of the [[Memphis State Tigers football|Memphis State Tigers]] of [[Memphis State University]] from 1973 to 1974.<ref name="Pfa"/> He was then a member of the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]] of the [[University of Miami]] from 1975 to 1977.<ref name="Pfa"/>

==Professional career==
Cesare signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) after going undrafted in the [[1978 NFL draft]].<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/c/cesa00200.html | title=Billy Cesare Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=12 May 2025}}</ref> He was released on September 7 but re-signed on September 11.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in ten games for the Buccaneers during the 1978 season, recovering one fumble, before being placed on injured reserve on November 30, 1978.<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CesaWi20.htm | title=William Cesare | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=12 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="transactions"/> Cesare appeared in all 16 games in 1979 and also two postseason games.<ref name="Pfr"/> He became a free agent after the 1979 season.<ref name="transactions"/> He mostly played [[special teams]] during his time with the Buccaneers.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bucpower.com/billy-cesare.htm | title=Billy Cesare | publisher=BucPower.com | accessdate=12 May 2025}}</ref>

Cesare was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]] on March 28, 1980.<ref name="transactions"/> He voluntarily left the team on August 20, 1980, stating he did not want to play football anymore.<ref name="Quit">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-akron-beacon-journal/172249007/ | title=Cesare leaves' Browns camp | work=[[The Akron Beacon Journal]] | date=August 21, 1980 | accessdate=12 May 2025 | author=Yannucci, Ray | pages=B8}}</ref> He was waived by the Browns on August 21, 1980.<ref name="Quit"/>

Cesare later signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] on December 11, 1980.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in two games for the Dolphins during the 1980 season.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was released on February 1, 1981.<ref name="transactions"/>

Cesare signed with the Buccaneers again on May 1, 1981.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in all 16 regular-season games in 1981 and also one playoff game.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was released on September 6, 1982.<ref name="transactions"/>

Cesare was signed by the [[Detroit Lions]] on November 19, 1982.<ref name="transactions"/> He was placed on injured reserve  on December 1 and later activated on December 31, 1982.<ref name="transactions"/> Overall, he appeared in two regular-season games and one postseason game in 1982.<ref name="Pfr"/> Cesare became a free agent after the 1982 season.<ref name="transactions"/>

Cesare signed with the [[Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) on February 28, 1983.<ref name="transactions"/> He started all 18 games for the Stallions during the [[1983 USFL season]], recording four interceptions for 52 yards, as Birmingham finished the season 9–9.<ref name="Pfa"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/1983usflbir.html | title=1983 Birmingham Stallions (USFL) | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=12 May 2025}}</ref>

Cesare played in eight games, starting one, for the [[Jacksonville Bulls]] of the USFL in 1984 and posted one sack.<ref name="Pfa"/> He was waived on April 24, 1984.<ref name="transactions"/>

Cesare was claimed off waivers by the [[Pittsburgh Maulers (1984)|Pittsburgh Maulers]] on April 25, 1984.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on April 28, 1984, before appearing in any games.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfa"/>

Cesare signed with the USFL's [[New Jersey Generals]] on May 9, 1984.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in seven games for the Generals in 1984.<ref name="Pfa"/> He was released on February 11, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/>

==Personal life==
Cesare became a horse trainer after his football career.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times/172251620/ | title=Cesare May Tackle the Derby | work=[[The Los Angeles Times]] | date=February 14, 2004 | accessdate=12 May 2025 | author=Christine, Bill | pages=D7}}</ref>

He was previously married to tennis player Allegra Pero, the daughter of tennis player [[George Pero]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-cleveland-press/172248595/ | title=Hail, Cesare | work=[[The Cleveland Press]] | date=August 16, 1980 | accessdate=12 May 2025 | author=Braham, Jim | pages=A40}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Johnston |first1=Joey |title=A love for the game leads to Cheval pro's return |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-tampa-tribune-a-love-for-the-game-le/140136929/ |access-date=February 3, 2024 |work=The Tampa Tribune |date=December 9, 1992 |at=5-Citrus}}</ref>

'''Billy Ray Bell''' (born January 16, 1961) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] for two seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Houston Oilers]] and [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. He played  [[college football]] for the [[Lamar Cardinals football|Lamar Cardinals]]. He also played for the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) and the [[Dallas Texans (arena)|Dallas Texans]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL).

==Early life and college==
Billy Ray Bell was born on January 16, 1961, in [[Dayton, Texas]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/b/bell00700.html | title=Billy Bell | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref> He attended [[Dayton High School (Texas)|Dayton High School]] in Dayton.<ref name="Pfa"/>

Bell was a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Lamar Cardinals football|Lamar Cardinals]] of [[Lamar University]] from 1983 to 1985.<ref name="Pfa"/>

==Professional career==
Bell signed with the [[Houston Oilers]] on May 4, 1989.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/bell00700.html | title=Billy Bell Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref> He was released on September 5, signed to the practice squad on September 8, promoted to the active roster on November 4, released again on November 21, signed to the practice squad again on November 24, and promoted to the active roster again on December 8, 1989.<ref name="transactions"/> Overall, he played in four games for the Oilers during the 1989 season.<ref name="Pfr"/> Bell also appeared in one playoff game that year.<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellBi21.htm | title=Billy Bell | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref>

Bell dressed in four games for the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] in 1990, recording ten tackles and one interception.<ref name="Pfa"/>

Bell was signed by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on May 5, 1991.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on August 27, re-signed on September 11, released again on October 1, and re-signed again on October 4.<ref name="transactions"/> Overall, he played in eight games, starting one, for the Chiefs in 1991 and made one interception.<ref name="Pfr"/> Bell was placed on injured reserve on November 16, 1991.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on January 2, 1992.<ref name="transactions"/>

Bell signed with the Oilers again on May 19, 1992, but was later released on August 31, 1992.<ref name="transactions"/>

He played in two games for the [[Dallas Texans (arena)|Dallas Texans]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) in 1993, totaling four solo tackles and four assisted tackles.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.arenafan.com/players/Billy_Bell-104/ | title=Billy Bell | publisher=ArenaFan.com | accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref><ref name="Pfa"/>

Bell signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the CFL in 1994 but was later released.<ref name="transactions"/>

He was signed by the [[Las Vegas Sting]] of the AFL in 1995 but was later released.<ref name="transactions"/>

'''Billy Bowman Jr.''' (born January 29, 2003) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]] and was selected by the Falcons in the fourth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
Bowman Jr. attended [[Billy Ryan High School]] in [[Denton, Texas]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Hoyt | first=Joseph | title=Billy Bowman Jr. said Denton Ryan would be back. With his proclamation fulfilled, the Raiders have another title shot. | website=Dallas News | date=2021-01-09 | url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/football/2021/01/08/denton-ryan-will-appear-in-state-championship-game-for-second-straight-year-after-defeating-mansfield-summit/ | access-date=2025-07-25}}</ref> He played defensive back and [[wide receiver]] in high school. As a senior, he had 86 receptions for 1,207 yards and 15 [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Crittenden | first=Jesse | title='It's really built my confidence': Bowman finding new role after disjointed freshman season | website=Norman Transcript | date=2022-04-12 | url=https://www.normantranscript.com/sports/its-really-built-my-confidence-bowman-finding-new-role-after-disjointed-freshman-season/article_5068aa7e-baa2-11ec-99bd-0b1ec8228993.html | access-date=2025-07-25}}</ref> He was selected to play in the 2021 [[Under Armour All-America Game]]. Bowman Jr. originally committed to play college football at the [[Texas Longhorns football|University of Texas at Austin]] before switching to the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|University of Oklahoma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/football/2020/11/01/after-decommitting-from-texas-denton-ryan-star-billy-bowman-jr-commits-to-oklahoma/|title=After decommitting from Texas, Denton Ryan star Billy Bowman Jr. commits to rival Oklahoma|date=2 November 2020 |publisher=The Dallas Morning News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/college/sooners/2020/11/03/ou-football-four-star-recruit-billy-bowman-jr-finds-the-best-fit-in-committing-to-sooners/307982007/|title=OU football: Four-star recruit Billy Bowman Jr. finds 'the best fit' in committing to Sooners|publisher=The Oklahoman}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2473090/2021/03/24/oklahoma-do-it-all-freshman-billy-bowman-jr-can-impact-sooners-in-many-ways-but-hes-starting-with-defense/|title=Oklahoma do-it-all freshman Billy Bowman Jr. can impact Sooners in many ways, but he's starting with defense|publisher=The Athletic}}</ref>

== College career ==
As a true freshman at Oklahoma in 2021, Bowman Jr. started seven of 11 games and had 22 tackles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/columns/berry-tramel/2022/04/11/ou-football-billy-bowman-not-ready-two-way-path-deion-sanders/7274852001/|title=Tramel's ScissorTales: Billy Bowman not ready to attempt the two-way path of Deion Sanders|publisher=The Oklahoman}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2022, he played in 11 games with nine starts and recorded 60 tackles and three interceptions. He returned to Oklahoma as a starter in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/ou/quiet-leader-billy-bowman-named-permanent-captain-for-ou-players-have-tremendous-respect-for-him/article_41e7a616-88ba-11ee-9426-5bd046cbc52c.html|title=Quiet leader Billy Bowman named permanent captain for OU: 'Players have tremendous respect for him'|date=22 November 2023 |publisher=Tulsa World}}</ref>

'''William Henry Davis Jr.''' (born December 6, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for one season with the [[Arizona Cardinals|St. Louis Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]]. He was also a member of the [[Denver Broncos]].

==Early life==
William Henry Davis Jr. was born on December 6, 1961, in [[Alexandria, Virginia]].<ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/d/davi03800.html | title=Billy Davis | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=26 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Mount Vernon High School (Virginia)|Mount Vernon High School]] in Alexandria.<ref name="pfa"/>

==College career==
Davis was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] from 1980 to 1983 as a [[defensive back]].<ref name="pfa"/><ref name="sr"/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-times-and-democrat/141365810/ | title=What's wrong? Tiger defender acknowledges frustration, sees tests ahead | work=The Times and Democrat | date=October 19, 1983 | accessdate=February 18, 2024}}</ref> He returned 12 punts for 45 yards his freshman year in 1980.<ref name="sr"/> He totaled 31 punt returns for 217 yards while also intercepting two passes in 1981.<ref name="sr"/> His 31 punt returns were the most in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] that season.<ref name="sr"/> The [[1981 Clemson Tigers football team|1981 Tigers]] were named consensus national champions. Davis recorded 24 punt returns for 160 yards, and three interceptions his junior year in 1982.<ref name="sr"/> As a senior in 1983, he returned 17 punts for 83 yards and also made two interceptions.<ref name="sr">{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/billy-davis-5.html?__hstc=223721476.67e94405d2ebe106ca6fd22b5112c332.1735218278222.1735229363341.1735235968061.4&__hssc=223721476.1.1735235968061&__hsfp=3011104808 | title=Billy Davis | publisher=sports-reference.com | accessdate=26 December 2024}}</ref> He graduated with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in sociology.<ref name="bio"/> He later served on the Clemson Club regional board of directors from the late 1990s to the early 2000s, and re-joined the board in 2021.<ref name="bio"/>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1984 NFL draft]], Davis signed with the [[Denver Broncos]] on May 2, 1984.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released by the Broncos on July 20, 1984.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/d/davi03800.html | title=Billy Davis NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=26 December 2024}}</ref>

He was signed by the [[Arizona Cardinals|St. Louis Cardinals]] on December 5, 1984, and played in one game for the team during the 1984 season.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaviBi22.htm | title=Billy Davis | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=26 December 2024}}</ref> He was released on August 26, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/> He was listed as a linebacker while with the Cardinals.<ref name="pfr"/>

==Post-football career==
Davis earned postgraduate degrees from [[Johns Hopkins University]] and [[Harvard University]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web | url=https://clemsonclub.org/board/billy-davis-84/ | title=Billy Davis ‘84 | publisher=clemsonclub.org | accessdate=26 December 2024}}</ref> He was a special agent in the [[United States Secret Service]] for 27 years until retiring in 2015.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="post">{{cite web | url=https://www.postandcourier.com/news/trump-shooting-secret-service-billy-davis-clemson/article_5efcf9c2-4377-11ef-a7fb-43d57f229a96.html | title=Former Secret Service agent, Clemson football player explains Trump shooting and fallout | publisher=postandcourier.com | date=July 16, 2024 | accessdate=26 December 2024 | author=Hamilton, Scott}}</ref> He was the special agent in charge of the Vice Presidential Protective Division for [[Joe Biden]].<ref name="bio"/><ref name="post"/>

He was on the board of directors for the [[Military Bowl]] from 2010 to 2018.<ref name="bio"/> He has also served as the director of executive and major event security for [[Samaritan’s Purse]] and the [[Billy Graham Evangelistic Association]].<ref name="bio"/>

'''Williams James Singletary''' (born March 18, 1951) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[New York Giants]] of [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Temple University]].<ref name=pfr>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SingBi20.htm |title=Bill Singletary Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |access-date=2026-04-07}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/players/bill-singletary/ |title=Bill Singletary, LB |work=Nfl.com |access-date=2026-04-07}}</ref>

Singletary played both [[offensive tackle]] and [[defensive tackle]] at [[Eastside High School (Camden, New Jersey)|Woodrow Wilson High School]] in [[Camden, New Jersey]].<ref name=hof/> He was an all-South Jersey team while there.<ref name=hof/>  Singletary was primarily an [[offensive guard]] in college.<ref name=battle>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=Philadelphia Daily News|author=Greenday, Joe|title=Bill Singletary wins his battle but Owls victims in grid 'war'|date=October 25, 1971|page=60|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/philadelphia-daily-news/195609275/}}</ref><ref name=weiss>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=Courier-Post|author=Weiss, Dick|title=Football magazines don't skip Singletary|date=August 21, 1972|page=28|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/courier-post/195609552/}}</ref><ref name=signed/> In 1971 he was named to the [[United Press International|UPI]] all-East college football team.<ref>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=Philadelphia Inquirer|title=All-East topped by Marinaro and Mitchell|date=November 24, 1971|page=23|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-philadelphia-inquirer/195608877/}}</ref>  He was named to the UPI All-American 2nd team as a guard for the 1972 season.<ref name=bannon>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=Philadelphia Inquirer|title=Bannon is named to All-America|date=December 7, 1972|page=34|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-philadelphia-inquirer/195608650/}}</ref> He was also named to several magazine All-American teams that season.<ref name=hof/>

Even while starring as a guard in college, there were concerns that Singletary was too small to play guard in the NFL.<ref name=weiss/> He was drafted as a linebacker by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the 4th round of the [[1973 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=Gettysburg Times|title=Eagles select offensive strength; Pittsburgh picks 'Who?' as defensive back|date=January 31, 1973|page=17|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gettysburg-times/195610118/}}</ref> He signed with the Chargers in July 1973.<ref name=signed>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=York Dispatch|title=Ex-Temple grid star signed by San Diego|date=July 10, 1973|page=20|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-york-dispatch/195610376/}}</ref> He was cut by the Chargers without playing a regular season game. He was signed by the [[New England Patriots]] before the 1974 season but was placed on [[injured reserve]] prior to the start of the season.<ref>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=Transcript-Telegram|title=Pat's down to 47-player limit|date=September 12, 1974|page=24|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/transcript-telegram/195611076/}}</ref> The Giants signed him as a free agent in December 1974 and he played 3 games for them during the remainder of the season.<ref name=pfr/><ref>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=Star-Ledger|author=Klein, Dave|title=Redskins' playoff chances still look good|date=December 1, 1974|page=Section 5, page 8|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-star-ledger/195611307/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|newspaper=Bridgeport Telegram|title=Injuries put damper on Giants' chances|author=Putrimas, Peter|date=November 28, 1974|page=59|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/bridgeport-telegram/195611779/}}</ref> He was cut by the Giants during the 1975 preseason.<ref>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2026-04-15|title=Hunter hitting the mark|newspaper=Mount Vernon Argus|date=August 4, 1975|page=17|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/mount-vernon-argus/195611538/}}</ref> He played for the [[Philadelphia Bell]] of the [[World Football League|WFL]] in 1975.<ref name=hof>{{cite web|title=Bill Singletary|accessdate=2026-04-15|url=https://owlsports.com/honors/hall-of-fame/bill-singletary/164|publisher=Temple University}}</ref>

Temple University retired Singletary's number 64 after the 1972 season.<ref name=hof/> He was inducted into Temple's Hall of Fame in 1984.<ref name=hof/>
